text: The mountain does not meet you halfway. You climbed, and it held still — that is the whole of the exchange, and Isa sits in it. Ice keeps its shape by refusing to move, and the summit has been refusing for longer than anyone has stood on it. Gebo asks what passes between two, and here one side gives stone and cold air and a view that was there before you, and you give the weight of standing. Neither hurries the other. The wind takes your warmth. The rock takes nothing, and offers the same.

You give your weight to wet sand, the sand gives it back through your soles, and neither of you asks the other to stay. The stones shine while they are wet. Behind you the prints are already softening.
